purpose: Starts sign-in with an identity provider such as Google, Apple or GitHub, carrying the provider's mark. Stack them above the email form, or lay the icon-only form in a row.

notFor.case: Submitting an email and password form.
Any action that is not signing in with a provider.

Default.visual: white: Surface/page fill, Border/control edge, Content/primary label, Elevation/highlight. brand: the provider's own action fill and on-action ink (social tokens).

Hover.visual: white: Surface/layer-1 fill, Border/control-hover edge. brand: the provider's hover fill.

Pressed.visual: white: Surface/muted fill, Border/control-hover edge. brand: the provider's pressed fill.

Focused.visual: The Default look plus a ring in the provider's focus colour (social token), not the shared ring roles.

Disabled.meaning: Sign-in with this provider is unavailable.
Disabled.visual: Action/disabled/default fill, Border/subtle edge, Content/disabled label.

a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches it; Enter or Space starts the sign-in (native button).
notes: Full width shows "Continue with <brand>"; the icon-only form takes an aria-label set from the brand.

openQuestions: Appearance names differ: Figma has outline · solid, code has white · brand. Which names are right? (Figma owns anatomy.)
Contrast: brand fills use each provider's own colours (social tokens with no Figma role name). Is AA promised for every provider, or do providers' brand rules win?
Status: spec/figma-components.status.json marks SocialLoginButton as rebuild. Which parts of this intent will change with the rebuild?
Order: should the provider order be fixed by the system, or only kept consistent by each product?
